text:
University College London (UCL) was founded on February 11, 1826, as London University, an alternative to the Anglican universities of Oxford and Cambridge. While philosopher Jeremy Bentham is commonly seen as its "spiritual father," his direct involvement was limited to purchasing a share. The institution's first warden, Leonard Horner, was a scientist, and classes in medicine began in 1828, with a teaching hospital opening in 1834.
UCL formally incorporated under the name University College, London, on November 28, 1836. It became the first British university to grant degrees to women in 1878, admitting them to the faculties of Arts and Law and Science that same year. UCL was reconstituted under the University of London Act 1898, and it ultimately gained its own university status in 2023. The university is a member of the Russell Group and is known for its large research output, with notable centers like the London Centre for Nanotechnology.
